title: View of the Cerro from the roof of the Mint
creator: Hiram Bingham (photograph)
why_public_domain: Published in the US in 1911; public domain in the US (all US works published before 1929 are). Note: Bingham died in 1956, so countries with a life+70 term treat it as protected until the end of 2026.

caption: The Cerro Rico of Potosí rising behind the vaulted roofs of the colonial Casa de Moneda, photographed by Hiram Bingham on his 1906–07 journey. It is a 20th-century photograph, not a view from the 1545 rush, but the mountain's cone-shaped silhouette is the one the first miners knew.

caption: The Cerro seen across one of the artificial lakes the Spanish built in the hills above Potosí to drive the stamp mills that crushed silver ore. Photographed in 1906–07, long after the boom, the reservoir is a surviving piece of the colonial mining works.

title: Facsimile of Davy's laboratory note of 19 October [1807] on the decomposition of potash
creator: Humphry Davy (manuscript); facsimile engraved for J. A. Paris
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).

caption: Davy's own hurried notes, dated 19 October, on passing current through potash in a tube with a platinum wire. They end by recording the decomposition of potash, the experiment that gave him potassium in 1807. This is an 1831 printed facsimile of the page, not the notebook itself.

This is a simplified 1896 redrawing, not Gillray's coloured original.

title: The Way They Go to California
creator: Nathaniel Currier (lithographer; OpenStax credits Currier & Ives)

caption: A New York cartoon from 1849 mocking gold fever: crowds with picks and shovels leap for a departing ship while others fly to California by airship and rocket. It is satire made on the East Coast, not a picture of the diggings.

title: San Francisco harbor, 1851
creator: Unknown daguerreotypist
why_public_domain: Photograph made in 1851; public domain worldwide. Reproduced in OpenStax U.S. History (credit: Library of Congress).
original_holder: Library of Congress (as credited by OpenStax); small low-resolution copy, 390 px wide
caption: San Francisco's harbour crowded with masts in early 1851. Many of the ships had been abandoned by crews who left for the goldfields, and the town had grown from a few hundred people to tens of thousands in about two years.

caption: Hangtown (later Placerville), a mining camp about ten miles from Coloma, as a forty-niner remembered it forty years on: tents, log cabins and miners with picks and pans on every slope. It is a later drawing from memory, not a view made in 1849.

creator: Unknown photographer

creator: Unknown photographer

title: Fig. 1: apparatus for absorbing nitrogen with red-hot magnesium
creator: William Ramsay (figure in his book)
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).

title: Fig. 3: electric-discharge flask for preparing argon on a large scale

why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).

caption: Rayleigh's method for making argon in quantity: an electric flame between platinum wires inside a large glass globe forces air's nitrogen to combine with oxygen, and caustic soda absorbs the result. The gas left over is argon.
